findings.evidence: The statement is `(a:R) * (x * (b:R) * y) = (c:R) * (x*y)`; the only reordered factor is `(b:R)`, which is central in every ring.
findings.fix: Generalize the signature to `[Ring R]` and prove the rearrangement using associativity and centrality of integer casts.
findings.issue: `intCast_mul_mul_mul_eq_intCast_mul` assumes `[CommRing R]`, but only commutation of integer casts with ring elements is needed.

findings.evidence: Lines 177–224 define and manipulate only `(coordinateCoeff j p : R) * Y ...`; all coefficients come from `ℤ`, hence commute with every element in an arbitrary ring.
findings.fix: Use `[Ring R]` for the coordinate definition and these lemmas, introducing stronger assumptions only at consumers that genuinely require them.
findings.issue: The file-wide `[CommRing R]` over-specializes `quotientCoordinate` and its generic API (`quotientCoordinate_def`, `_add`, `_smul`, `_map_intCast`, and `_eq_of_isStep`); these are sums of entries with central integer coefficients and need no commutativity of arbitrary elements.

summary: Two reusable coordinate/cast APIs unnecessarily require commutative rings although their formulas only use central integer casts and work over arbitrary rings.
